## The lesson

A CPU-advance liveness probe must walk the **descendant tree** (recursive
`pgrep -P`), not a session set (`pgrep -s`), whenever the watched workload
spawns children with `start_new_session=True` / `setsid`. Session-scoped probes
are correct only for trees that stay in one session — which is exactly what the
Step 9c gate itself was (its worker was visible to `pgrep -s`, which is why the
same arm correctly proved the gate healthy through its 10-minute quiet stretch
at 2,982 CPU-seconds).

Two probes, two scopes, and the workload decides which is valid:

| workload | children | valid CPU probe |
|---|---|---|
| Step 9c gate pytest | same session | `pgrep -s` (worked) |
| compare pristine runs | `start_new_session=True` | recursive `pgrep -P` (required) |

Note the irony worth keeping: `setsid` is the very mechanism the detached-launch
convention mandates for durability, so ANY probe of a properly-detached workload
inherits this blindness unless it walks children explicitly.
